root_cause.text: `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` in `mm/slub.c` failed to reject NMI context on UP kernels, so its internal `spin_trylock()` could re-enter SLUB and “succeed” on an already-held `n->list_lock`, corrupting slab state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` guard with the comment “On UP, spin_trylock() always succeeds even when it is locked,” and the CVE description explains that NMI callers could re-enter the slab allocator and acquire `n->list_lock` already held by the interrupted context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` in NMI context on UP kernels to avoid incorrect locking behavior.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added in `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` before the `retry:` label: on non-SMP builds, if execution is in NMI context, the function now returns `NULL`. A comment was also added explaining that on UP systems `spin_trylock()` always succeeds even when locked.
intent_record.how: This prevents `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` from proceeding in NMI context on uniprocessor kernels, avoiding behavior that would rely on `spin_trylock()` semantics that do not provide exclusion on UP. As a result, allocation is denied in a case where the locking logic would be ineffective or unsafe.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds rejection of kmalloc_nolock_noprof() in NMI context on UP kernels to prevent re-entrant locking of SLUB's list_lock.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix guard only rejected NMI/hardirq on PREEMPT_RT, leaving UP kernels unprotected. As a result, kmalloc_nolock_noprof() could run in NMI context on UP and re-enter SLUB's locking path incorrectly.

vuln_statements.explanation: This guard only blocked NMI/hardirq on PREEMPT_RT, so on UP kernels kmalloc_nolock_noprof() could still run in NMI context and re-enter SLUB while n->list_lock was already held, leading to slab state corruption.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this version. The root cause was that kmalloc_nolock_noprof() failed to reject NMI context on UP kernels, allowing re-entry into SLUB via an internal trylock path. In this snippet, that guard is explicitly added: `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq())) return NULL;` and the old context-dependent NMI avoidance logic is removed. The old problematic path that conditionally skipped `__slab_alloc_node()` based on `in_nmi()`/`local_lock_is_locked()` is gone; instead the code unconditionally calls `ret = __slab_alloc_node(s, alloc_gfp, node, _RET_IP_, size);`. This commit therefore already contains the fix, not the bug.
